feed.title: Indian Railways Expands Passenger Connectivity and Freight Capacity in August 2026; Freight Loading Grows by 5.4% Over August 2025
feed.summary: August 2026 witnessed significant expansion in railway connectivity and services across the country, with Indian Railways recording growth in both passenger movement and freight loading. During the month, 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised, providing more affordable and comfortable travel options to passengers across several important routes, while 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) were commissioned to improve last-mile freight connectivity for industries. Indian Railways also recorded 5.4 per cent growth in freight loading, reflecting continued demand from key sectors of the economy. Passenger traffic increased as well, with additional special train services being operated to meet the surge in demand during the festival season. Indian Railways loaded 137.9 million tonnes of freight during August 2026, compared to 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025, registering a 5.4 per cent year-on-year growth.

feed.title: 50 Kilometres, Countless Beneficiaries: Mizoram’s Railway Lifeline Completes One Year of Success
feed.summary: On 13 th September 2025, the inauguration of the 51.38 km Bairabi-Sairang railway line and the Sairang Railway station by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, opened a new chapter of progress and development for Mizoram. Within just one year, the railway line has brought about transformative development in this remote hill state, and has transformed from just a line on the railway map into a gateway towards improved mobility, greater access to markets, enhanced tourism and new opportunities. For generations, Mizoram’s difficult terrain made long-distance movement heavily dependent on roads, making travel very time consuming, uncomfortable and unrealiable. The commissioning of the Bairabi-Sairang new railway line completed changed the scenario.

pib-2309663.title: Indian Railways Expands Passenger Connectivity and Freight Capacity in August 2026; Freight Loading Grows by 5.4% Over August 2025
pib-2309663.summary: August 2026 witnessed significant expansion in railway connectivity and services across the country, with Indian Railways recording growth in both passenger movement and freight loading. During the month, 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised, providing more affordable and comfortable travel options to passengers across several important routes, while 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) were commissioned to improve last-mile freight connectivity for industries. Indian Railways also recorded 5.4 per cent growth in freight loading, reflecting continued demand from key sectors of the economy. Passenger traffic increased as well, with additional special train services being operated to meet the surge in demand during the festival season. Indian Railways loaded 137.9 million tonnes of freight during August 2026, compared to 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025, registering a 5.4 per cent year-on-year growth.

pib-2309650.title: 50 Kilometres, Countless Beneficiaries: Mizoram’s Railway Lifeline Completes One Year of Success
pib-2309650.summary: On 13 th September 2025, the inauguration of the 51.38 km Bairabi-Sairang railway line and the Sairang Railway station by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, opened a new chapter of progress and development for Mizoram. Within just one year, the railway line has brought about transformative development in this remote hill state, and has transformed from just a line on the railway map into a gateway towards improved mobility, greater access to markets, enhanced tourism and new opportunities. For generations, Mizoram’s difficult terrain made long-distance movement heavily dependent on roads, making travel very time consuming, uncomfortable and unrealiable. The commissioning of the Bairabi-Sairang new railway line completed changed the scenario.

                              <h2 id="Titleh2">
                                    Indian Railways Expands Passenger Connectivity and Freight Capacity in August 2026; Freight Loading Grows by 5.4% Over August 2025
                              </h2>
                              <h3 id="Subtitleh3">
                                    <span id="ltrSubtitle"><br/>14 Services of Amrit Bharat regularised to Strengthen Affordable Rail Connectivity; Services Link Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Other Key Regions in August 2026<br/><br/>5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals Commissioned, Taking Total to 149; Faster Freight Movement to Support Industry and Regional Economic Activity </span>
                              </h3>
                        </div>

                        <div id="PrDateTime" class="ReleaseDateSubHeaddateTime text-center pt20">
                              Posted On:
                13 SEP 2026 12:06PM by PIB Delhi
                        </div>
                        
                        <div class='pt20'>
                        </div>
                        <input type="hidden" name="hydphotoUrl" id="hydphotoUrl" />
                        
                        <p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">August 2026 witnessed significant expansion in railway connectivity and services across the country, with Indian Railways recording growth in both passenger movement and freight loading. During the month, 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised, providing more affordable and comfortable travel options to passengers across several important routes, while 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) were commissioned to improve last-mile freight connectivity for industries.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways also recorded 5.4 per cent growth in freight loading, reflecting continued demand from key sectors of the economy. Passenger traffic increased as well, with additional special train services being operated to meet the surge in demand during the festival season.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>More Freight Movement, Supporting Industry and the Economy</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways loaded 137.9 million tonnes of freight during August 2026, compared to 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025, registering a 5.4 per cent year-on-year growth.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The increase in freight movement reflects growing demand from key sectors such as coal, iron ore, steel, fertilizers and other commodities. Higher rail freight movement also helps industries access reliable transportation while supporting the movement of essential commodities across regions.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Freight revenue during August 2026 increased by 6.27 per cent compared to August 2025, indicating continued strengthening of the freight business of Indian Railways.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Higher Movement of Key Commodities Supports Industry and Essential Supply Chains</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Several important commodity groups recorded healthy growth during August 2026. Iron Ore loading increased by 12.1 per cent, Clinker by 10.4 per cent, Domestic Container by 9.2 per cent and Coal by 6 per cent. Finished Steel loading increased by 4.9 per cent, Mineral Oil by 3.1 per cent, Fertilizers by 1.6 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 8.2 per cent.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The growth in these segments strengthens the rail-based supply chain for industries and supports the movement of essential inputs and finished goods across the country. Increased container movement, in particular, supports more efficient transportation of diverse goods through the rail network.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to Improve Freight Connectivity</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">In August 2026, 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals were commissioned, taking the cumulative number of commissioned GCTs to 149 as on 31 August 2026.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The newly commissioned terminals are at - </span></span></p>

<ul>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Shivlakha, Gujarat</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Nalli, Tamil Nadu</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Shaktinagar, Uttar Pradesh</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Deoragram, Madhya Pradesh</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Brajrajnagar ,  Odisha</span></span></p>
	</li>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The expansion of the Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal network brings freight-handling facilities closer to production and consumption centres. By enabling more direct and efficient handling of goods, these terminals can reduce avoidable movement, improve logistics efficiency and facilitate faster evacuation of freight from industrial and commercial locations.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The growing GCT network is also helping strengthen the integration of railways with India's wider logistics infrastructure, giving industries greater access to rail-based freight transportation.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>14 Services of Amrit Bharat were regularised to Expand Affordable Rail Connectivity</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">August 2026 marked a significant expansion of passenger connectivity, with 14  Amrit Bharat services were regularised from special train to regular train during the month, taking the total number of Amrit Bharat services to 86.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The services connect several major cities and regions, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and other important parts of the country.</span></span></p>

<ul>

	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Subedarganj - Lokmanya Tilak Terminus</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Gorakhpur - Bandra Terminus</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Gorakhpur - Delhi Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Ahmedabad - Bhagalpur</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Lokmanya Tilak Terminus - Prayagraj Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Prayagraj Jn - Udhna Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Dhanbad - Coimbatore, among others.</span></span></p>
	</li>
</ul>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">These new services are expected to provide passengers with more travel options, improved connectivity between major urban centres & regional destinations and affordable long-distance rail travel.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">For Purvanchal and eastern Uttar Pradesh, services from Gorakhpur to Bandra Terminus and Delhi provide additional connectivity to two major metropolitan regions, benefiting passengers travelling for employment, education, business and family purposes.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Similarly, the Ahmedabad-Bhagalpur connectivity strengthens the rail link between Gujarat and Bihar, providing passengers from both regions with another direct travel option. The Dhanbad-Coimbatore service improves long-distance connectivity between eastern India and southern India, particularly benefiting passengers travelling between industrial and employment centres.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Connectivity between Prayagraj and Udhna and between Prayagraj and Mumbai further expands travel options for passengers from Uttar Pradesh travelling towards western India.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The expansion of Amrit Bharat services is part of Indian Railways' continued efforts to provide comfortable, affordable and accessible long-distance rail travel, particularly for passengers travelling between major cities and emerging regional centres.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Passenger Traffic Continues to Grow</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways carried 67.27 crore passengers during August 2026, compared to 64.43 crore passengers during August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Suburban passenger traffic recorded particularly strong growth, increasing by 9.02 per cent. A total of 38.01 crore suburban passengers travelled during August 2026, compared to 34.89 crore in August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The increase reflects the continued importance of the railway network in providing affordable daily mobility to millions of passengers, particularly in densely populated urban and suburban regions.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Additional Special Trains Help Passengers During Festival Rush</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">With increased passenger demand during the festival season, Indian Railways operated 144 trips of Rakshabandhan Special trains between 25 and 31 August 2026, compared to 48 trips operated between 8 and 14 August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The substantial increase in special train services helped provide additional travel capacity during the peak festival period, giving passengers more options to travel during a period of exceptionally high demand.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Such additional services are particularly important for passengers travelling to their hometowns and families during festivals, helping ease pressure on regular services and improving travel availability during peak periods.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Expanding Rail Connectivity, Strengthening Everyday Mobility</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The developments during August 2026 reflect Indian Railways' continued focus on expanding passenger connectivity, improving travel options, strengthening freight infrastructure and responding to changing demand.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The introduction of new Amrit Bharat services is expanding affordable long-distance connectivity between major cities and regional centres, while additional festival services are helping passengers manage seasonal travel demand. At the same time, the expansion of Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals is strengthening the logistics network and improving rail access for industries.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Through continued capacity augmentation, improved operational efficiency and expansion of passenger and freight infrastructure, Indian Railways remains focused on making rail travel more accessible and strengthening the railway network as an important driver of economic activity and regional connectivity across the country.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The developments during August 2026 reflect Indian Railways' continued focus on expanding passenger connectivity, improving travel options, strengthening freight infrastructure and responding to changing demand.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The introduction of new Amrit Bharat services is expanding affordable long-distance connectivity between major cities and regional centres, while additional festival services are helping passengers manage seasonal travel demand. At the same time, the expansion of Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals is strengthening the logistics network and improving rail access for industries.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Through continued capacity augmentation, improved operational efficiency and expansion of passenger and freight infrastructure, Indian Railways remains focused on making rail travel more accessible and strengthening the railway network as an important driver of economic activity and regional connectivity across the country.</span></span></p>

            <input type="hidden" name="ltrSubtitlee" id="ltrSubtitlee" value="<br/>14 Services of Amrit Bharat regularised to Strengthen Affordable Rail Connectivity; Services Link Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Other Key Regions in August 2026<br/><br/>5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals Commissioned, Taking Total to 149; Faster Freight Movement to Support Industry and Regional Economic Activity&#160;" />
            <input type="hidden" name="ltrDescriptionn" id="ltrDescriptionn" value="<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">August 2026 witnessed significant expansion in railway connectivity and services across the country, with Indian Railways recording growth in both passenger movement and freight loading. During the month, 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised, providing more affordable and comfortable travel options to passengers across several important routes, while 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) were commissioned to improve last-mile freight connectivity for industries.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways also recorded 5.4 per cent growth in freight loading, reflecting continued demand from key sectors of the economy. Passenger traffic increased as well, with additional special train services being operated to meet the surge in demand during the festival season.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>More Freight Movement, Supporting Industry and the Economy</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways loaded 137.9 million tonnes of freight during August 2026, compared to 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025, registering a 5.4 per cent year-on-year growth.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The increase in freight movement reflects growing demand from key sectors such as coal, iron ore, steel, fertilizers and other commodities. Higher rail freight movement also helps industries access reliable transportation while supporting the movement of essential commodities across regions.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Freight revenue during August 2026 increased by 6.27 per cent compared to August 2025, indicating continued strengthening of the freight business of Indian Railways.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Higher Movement of Key Commodities Supports Industry and Essential Supply Chains</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Several important commodity groups recorded healthy growth during August 2026. Iron Ore loading increased by 12.1 per cent, Clinker by 10.4 per cent, Domestic Container by 9.2 per cent and Coal by 6 per cent. Finished Steel loading increased by 4.9 per cent, Mineral Oil by 3.1 per cent, Fertilizers by 1.6 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 8.2 per cent.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The growth in these segments strengthens the rail-based supply chain for industries and supports the movement of essential inputs and finished goods across the country. Increased container movement, in particular, supports more efficient transportation of diverse goods through the rail network.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to Improve Freight Connectivity</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">In August 2026, 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals were commissioned, taking the cumulative number of commissioned GCTs to 149 as on 31 August 2026.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The newly commissioned terminals are at - </span></span></p>

<ul>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Shivlakha, Gujarat</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Nalli, Tamil Nadu</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Shaktinagar, Uttar Pradesh</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Deoragram, Madhya Pradesh</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Brajrajnagar ,&nbsp; Odisha</span></span></p>
	</li>
</ul>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The expansion of the Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal network brings freight-handling facilities closer to production and consumption centres. By enabling more direct and efficient handling of goods, these terminals can reduce avoidable movement, improve logistics efficiency and facilitate faster evacuation of freight from industrial and commercial locations.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The growing GCT network is also helping strengthen the integration of railways with India&#39;s wider logistics infrastructure, giving industries greater access to rail-based freight transportation.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>14 Services of Amrit Bharat were regularised to Expand Affordable Rail Connectivity</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">August 2026 marked a significant expansion of passenger connectivity, with 14&nbsp; Amrit Bharat services were regularised from special train to regular train during the month, taking the total number of Amrit Bharat services to 86.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The services connect several major cities and regions, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and other important parts of the country.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The services include:</span></span></p>

<ul>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Subedarganj - Lokmanya Tilak Terminus</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Gorakhpur - Bandra Terminus</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Gorakhpur - Delhi Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Ahmedabad - Bhagalpur</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Lokmanya Tilak Terminus - Prayagraj Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Prayagraj Jn - Udhna Jn</span></span></p>
	</li>
	<li style="text-align:justify">
	<p><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Dhanbad - Coimbatore, among others.</span></span></p>
	</li>
</ul>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">These new services are expected to provide passengers with more travel options, improved connectivity between major urban centres &amp; regional destinations and affordable long-distance rail travel.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">For Purvanchal and eastern Uttar Pradesh, services from Gorakhpur to Bandra Terminus and Delhi provide additional connectivity to two major metropolitan regions, benefiting passengers travelling for employment, education, business and family purposes.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Similarly, the Ahmedabad-Bhagalpur connectivity strengthens the rail link between Gujarat and Bihar, providing passengers from both regions with another direct travel option. The Dhanbad-Coimbatore service improves long-distance connectivity between eastern India and southern India, particularly benefiting passengers travelling between industrial and employment centres.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Connectivity between Prayagraj and Udhna and between Prayagraj and Mumbai further expands travel options for passengers from Uttar Pradesh travelling towards western India.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The expansion of Amrit Bharat services is part of Indian Railways&#39; continued efforts to provide comfortable, affordable and accessible long-distance rail travel, particularly for passengers travelling between major cities and emerging regional centres.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Passenger Traffic Continues to Grow</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Indian Railways carried 67.27 crore passengers during August 2026, compared to 64.43 crore passengers during August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Suburban passenger traffic recorded particularly strong growth, increasing by 9.02 per cent. A total of 38.01 crore suburban passengers travelled during August 2026, compared to 34.89 crore in August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The increase reflects the continued importance of the railway network in providing affordable daily mobility to millions of passengers, particularly in densely populated urban and suburban regions.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Additional Special Trains Help Passengers During Festival Rush</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">With increased passenger demand during the festival season, Indian Railways operated 144 trips of Rakshabandhan Special trains between 25 and 31 August 2026, compared to 48 trips operated between 8 and 14 August 2025.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The substantial increase in special train services helped provide additional travel capacity during the peak festival period, giving passengers more options to travel during a period of exceptionally high demand.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Such additional services are particularly important for passengers travelling to their hometowns and families during festivals, helping ease pressure on regular services and improving travel availability during peak periods.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Expanding Rail Connectivity, Strengthening Everyday Mobility</strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The developments during August 2026 reflect Indian Railways&#39; continued focus on expanding passenger connectivity, improving travel options, strengthening freight infrastructure and responding to changing demand.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The introduction of new Amrit Bharat services is expanding affordable long-distance connectivity between major cities and regional centres, while additional festival services are helping passengers manage seasonal travel demand. At the same time, the expansion of Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals is strengthening the logistics network and improving rail access for industries.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">Through continued capacity augmentation, improved operational efficiency and expansion of passenger and freight infrastructure, Indian Railways remains focused on making rail travel more accessible and strengthening the railway network as an important driver of economic activity and regional connectivity across the country.</span></span></p>

<p style="margin-right:-; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px">*****</span></span></p>

                const festivalStart = new Date("2025-11-20T00:00:00").getTime();
                const festivalEnd = new Date("2025-11-28T23:59:59").getTime();

                const countdownElement = document.getElementById("countdown");

                const interval = setInterval(() => {
                      const now = new Date().getTime();

                      // BEFORE FESTIVAL — show days + hours left
                      if (now < festivalStart) {
                            const diff = festivalStart - now;
                            const days = Math.floor(diff / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));
                            const hours = Math.floor((diff % (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)) / (1000 * 60 * 60));

                            countdownElement.innerHTML = `
              ${days} Day${days !== 1 ? 's' : ''} 
              ${hours} Hour${hours !== 1 ? 's' : ''} to go
          `;

                      }

                      // DURING FESTIVAL — show 56th IFFI - Day X
                      else if (now >= festivalStart && now <= festivalEnd) {
                            const dayNumber = Math.floor((now - festivalStart) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)) + 1;
                            countdownElement.innerHTML = `56th IFFI - Day ${dayNumber}`;
                      }

                      // AFTER FESTIVAL — new message
                      else {
                            countdownElement.innerHTML = `✨ IFFI closes but never ends…`;

                            // Width change logic
                            const elements = document.querySelectorAll('.film-roll-badge');
                            elements.forEach(el => el.style.width = "350px");

                            clearInterval(interval);
                      }

                }, 1000);
          </script>

                        <p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">On 13<sup>th </sup>September 2025, the inauguration of the 51.38 km Bairabi-Sairang railway line and the Sairang Railway station by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, opened a new chapter of progress and development for Mizoram. Within just one year, the railway line has brought about transformative development in this remote hill state, and has transformed from just a line on the railway map into a gateway towards improved mobility, greater access to markets, enhanced tourism and new opportunities.</span></span></span></p>

<script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script>
</center>
<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>The Milestone: When the Rails Reached the Hills</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">For generations, Mizoram’s difficult terrain made long-distance movement heavily dependent on roads, making travel very time consuming, uncomfortable and unrealiable. The commissioning of the Bairabi-Sairang new railway line completed changed the scenario.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image001_20260913113014_5ed34d.jpg" style="height:289px; width:624px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The Bairabi-Sairang line carries the national railway network across Mizoram’s challenging hill terrain)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The Bairabi Sairang railway line is an engineering marvel, traversing the steep hills, deep valleys and gorges of Mizoram. The project comprises 153 bridges, including 55 major bridges, 88 minor bridges and 10 Road Over Bridges/Road Under Bridges. As many as six bridges exceed 70 meters in height, with the tallest rising up to 114 meters, which is 42 metres taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar. The alignment also passes through 45 tunnels stretching over almost 16 kilometres. The rail corridor connects the national railway network onwards from Bairabi with the four newly developed stations of Hortoki, Kawnpui, Mualkhang and finally the Sairang railway station, thereby completing rail connectivity to the very threshold of Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Thus, the inauguration of the Bairabi Sairang Railway Line on 13<sup>th </sup>September 2025 fulfilled a long cherished dream of the people of Mizoram, and brought reliable railway passenger and freight services close to the State’s largest centre of population, administration, education and commerce.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image002_20260913113026_aa1eb2.jpg" style="height:328px; width:511px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(Sairang station became Mizoram’s new passenger and logistics gateway to the national railway network)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong> </strong></span></span></h2>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Passenger Mobility: The Numbers tell a story of trust</strong></span></span></h2>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Three important long distance train services now connect the capital of Mizoram with the cities of Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The Sairang – Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram its first direct premium railway connection with the national capital, while the Guwahati and Kolkata services created dependable links with major educational, commercial and medical centres across the eastern and northern parts of the country. Further, the Sairang – Silchar passenger train service, which was inaugurated by Hon’ble Union Minister of Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in January 2026, provided a regular and reliable passenger train service connecting Sairang with the Barak Valley of Assam.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Over the course of the last one year, these train services have completed more than 1100 trips,  becoming an integral part of the lives of the people of Mizoram. The strongest endorsement of the importance of these train services have come from the passengers themselves, receiving the patronage of over 15 Lakh passengers. Passenger demand for these trains have consistently remained very high, with all trains running at over 100% capacity on every trip.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The tri – weekly train service from Sairang to Kolkata has recorded an average occupancy level of over 140 %, while occupany in the daily train service from Sairang to Guwahati has consistently stayed above 110%. The Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express has similarly achieved an average occupany of over 145 %. These train services have also generated total ticket sales of Rs 54 Crores for the Indian Railways.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">During this last one year, Sairang railway station has successfully catered to more than 5.54 lakh passenger movements, with an average of 3300 passengers visiting the station every day. The railway station has not only emerged as a vital hub for passenger travel, but also an integral part of community life in the surrounding area, with local residents carrying out tree plantations and other environmental initiatives around the station complex.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"> </p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image003_20260913113036_c172d1.jpg" style="height:235px; width:360px" /></span></span></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> <img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image004_20260913113047_aae92e.jpg" style="height:235px; width:347px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong> </strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>Freight Transformation: Rail Cargo to Aizawl</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The Bairabi Sairang Railway line has also brought about transformative change in freight transportation in Mizoram, enabling goods including essential commodities, automobiles and construction materials to reach Aizawl in a safe, time bound and cost effective manner.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The first railway cargo train arrived at Sairang on 14<sup>th </sup>September 2025, just one day after the inauguration of the new line, carrying a consignment of more than 26000 bags of cement from STAR Cement Siding at Tetelia near Guwahati. This cargo train had an immediate impact on the prices of cement in Aizawl, clearly demonstrating how railways can drastically reduce logistics costs and contribute to economic development of an entire region. Moreover the direct freight train services bridge the gap in procuring the automobiles, thus reducing the landing cost, making it more pocket friendly to the end consumers. In another notable milestone, the first automobile consignment, consisting of 119 Maruti cars from Changsari near Guwahati, arrived at Sairang by rail in December 2025, transforming automobile logistics in the region.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">In the last one year, more than 2500 wagons of railway freight have been delivered at Sairang. Of these, approximately 70% of the cargo consisted of construction materials like cement, stone and sand, These commodities have supported housing and public works in Mizoram, promoting infrastructure development in the state at lower costs as well as reducing the time required for materials to reach their destinations.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Other railway cargo at Sairang has consisted of essential commodities including rice and fertilizers, as well as 156 wagons containing automobiles.  Automobile rakes have created a safer and higher capacity supply channel for vehicles, while fertilizer and foodgrains have served agriculture and local PDS distribution in the state, shifting bulk movement from long road hauls to efficient railway transport.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image005_20260913113058_273e78.jpg" style="height:199px; width:339px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The inaugural cement rake established Sairang as a freight-handling point)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image006_20260913113107_16cbb4.jpg" style="height:251px; width:335px" /></strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The 1<sup>st</sup> Automobile Freight Rake handled at Mizoram)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> </span></span></span></p>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Railway enhances educational and tourism opportunities for people of Mizoram</strong></span></span></h2>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Direct trains from Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati and Silchar have made Mizoram easier to reach for domestic travellers. Railway has offered an affordable entry point for visitors who earlier had to depended entirely on air or lengthy road journeys. This has resulted in an overall growth of tourism in Mizoram by over 86% since the introduction of railways.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The benefits have extended beyond ticketed travel. Greater visitor movement is supporting hotels, homestays, restaurants, taxis, guides, cultural enterprises and local markets. Reliable rail access is also strengthening Mizoram’s ability to host educational, sporting, cultural and official events with wider national participation.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">For students of Mizoram, railway connectivity has expanded practical access to universities, professional institutes, coaching centres, examinations and academic events outside Mizoram.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>Local Enterprise: From Mizo Hands to National Markets</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Railways is also playing an empowering role for popularizing Mizoram’s handloom, bamboo, cane and craft traditions in wider markets. The first parcel consignment from Sairang was booked on 19<sup>th </sup>September 2025, carrying Anthurium flowers to Delhi through the parcel van of the Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express. That modest consignment carried a larger message: high-value local produce could begin its national journey from within Mizoram itself.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image007_20260913113117_497a17.jpg" style="height:199px; width:411px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The first parcel consignment of Anthurium flowers was booked from Sairang for Delhi)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image008_20260913113127_0db382.jpg" style="height:207px; width:427px" /></strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(Parcel space created a direct channel for delicate and time-sensitive local produce</strong>)</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> </span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>One Year and Beyond: From Isolation to New Possibilities</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">In one year, the Bairabi Sairang railway line has demonstrated the far reaching effects of the successful translation of vision into reality. The impact is visible in several directions at once. Passengers have direct access to major cities; students have a more practical route to institutions and examinations; tourists have an affordable gateway; traders receive bulk consignments closer to market; construction and food supplies move with greater capacity; and flowers, crafts and other local products gain a pathway towards national consumers.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The deeper significance of Sairang lies in what it has made possible. A railway line built through difficult hills has compressed distance, widened choice and given Mizoram a new logistics identity. It has linked mobility with dignity, infrastructure with enterprise, and connectivity with opportunity.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image009_20260913113138_4c89c0.jpg" style="height:237px; width:624px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The Sairang-AnandVihar Terminal Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram a direct premium connection with the national capital)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image010_20260913113150_cdff01.jpg" style="height:372px; width:496px" /></strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>(The Sairang Railway Bridge has a pier of height 114m, which is 42 m taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar)</strong></span></span></p>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong> </strong></span></span></h2>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Passenger Mobility: The Numbers tell a story of trust</strong></span></span></h2>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Three important long distance train services now connect the capital of Mizoram with the cities of Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The Sairang – Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram its first direct premium railway connection with the national capital, while the Guwahati and Kolkata services created dependable links with major educational, commercial and medical centres across the eastern and northern parts of the country. Further, the Sairang – Silchar passenger train service, which was inaugurated by Hon’ble Union Minister of Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in January 2026, provided a regular and reliable passenger train service connecting Sairang with the Barak Valley of Assam.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Over the course of the last one year, these train services have completed more than 1100 trips,  becoming an integral part of the lives of the people of Mizoram. The strongest endorsement of the importance of these train services have come from the passengers themselves, receiving the patronage of over 15 Lakh passengers. Passenger demand for these trains have consistently remained very high, with all trains running at over 100% capacity on every trip.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The tri – weekly train service from Sairang to Kolkata has recorded an average occupancy level of over 140 %, while occupany in the daily train service from Sairang to Guwahati has consistently stayed above 110%. The Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express has similarly achieved an average occupany of over 145 %. These train services have also generated total ticket sales of Rs 54 Crores for the Indian Railways.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">During this last one year, Sairang railway station has successfully catered to more than 5.54 lakh passenger movements, with an average of 3300 passengers visiting the station every day. The railway station has not only emerged as a vital hub for passenger travel, but also an integral part of community life in the surrounding area, with local residents carrying out tree plantations and other environmental initiatives around the station complex.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"> </p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image003_20260913113036_c172d1.jpg" style="height:235px; width:360px" /></span></span></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> <img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image004_20260913113047_aae92e.jpg" style="height:235px; width:347px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong> </strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>Freight Transformation: Rail Cargo to Aizawl</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The Bairabi Sairang Railway line has also brought about transformative change in freight transportation in Mizoram, enabling goods including essential commodities, automobiles and construction materials to reach Aizawl in a safe, time bound and cost effective manner.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The first railway cargo train arrived at Sairang on 14<sup>th </sup>September 2025, just one day after the inauguration of the new line, carrying a consignment of more than 26000 bags of cement from STAR Cement Siding at Tetelia near Guwahati. This cargo train had an immediate impact on the prices of cement in Aizawl, clearly demonstrating how railways can drastically reduce logistics costs and contribute to economic development of an entire region. Moreover the direct freight train services bridge the gap in procuring the automobiles, thus reducing the landing cost, making it more pocket friendly to the end consumers. In another notable milestone, the first automobile consignment, consisting of 119 Maruti cars from Changsari near Guwahati, arrived at Sairang by rail in December 2025, transforming automobile logistics in the region.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">In the last one year, more than 2500 wagons of railway freight have been delivered at Sairang. Of these, approximately 70% of the cargo consisted of construction materials like cement, stone and sand, These commodities have supported housing and public works in Mizoram, promoting infrastructure development in the state at lower costs as well as reducing the time required for materials to reach their destinations.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Other railway cargo at Sairang has consisted of essential commodities including rice and fertilizers, as well as 156 wagons containing automobiles.  Automobile rakes have created a safer and higher capacity supply channel for vehicles, while fertilizer and foodgrains have served agriculture and local PDS distribution in the state, shifting bulk movement from long road hauls to efficient railway transport.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image005_20260913113058_273e78.jpg" style="height:199px; width:339px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The inaugural cement rake established Sairang as a freight-handling point)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image006_20260913113107_16cbb4.jpg" style="height:251px; width:335px" /></strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The 1<sup>st</sup> Automobile Freight Rake handled at Mizoram)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> </span></span></span></p>

<h2 style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Railway enhances educational and tourism opportunities for people of Mizoram</strong></span></span></h2>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Direct trains from Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati and Silchar have made Mizoram easier to reach for domestic travellers. Railway has offered an affordable entry point for visitors who earlier had to depended entirely on air or lengthy road journeys. This has resulted in an overall growth of tourism in Mizoram by over 86% since the introduction of railways.  </span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The benefits have extended beyond ticketed travel. Greater visitor movement is supporting hotels, homestays, restaurants, taxis, guides, cultural enterprises and local markets. Reliable rail access is also strengthening Mizoram’s ability to host educational, sporting, cultural and official events with wider national participation.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">For students of Mizoram, railway connectivity has expanded practical access to universities, professional institutes, coaching centres, examinations and academic events outside Mizoram.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>Local Enterprise: From Mizo Hands to National Markets</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">Railways is also playing an empowering role for popularizing Mizoram’s handloom, bamboo, cane and craft traditions in wider markets. The first parcel consignment from Sairang was booked on 19<sup>th </sup>September 2025, carrying Anthurium flowers to Delhi through the parcel van of the Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express. That modest consignment carried a larger message: high-value local produce could begin its national journey from within Mizoram itself.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image007_20260913113117_497a17.jpg" style="height:199px; width:411px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The first parcel consignment of Anthurium flowers was booked from Sairang for Delhi)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image008_20260913113127_0db382.jpg" style="height:207px; width:427px" /></strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(Parcel space created a direct channel for delicate and time-sensitive local produce</strong>)</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"> </span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>One Year and Beyond: From Isolation to New Possibilities</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">In one year, the Bairabi Sairang railway line has demonstrated the far reaching effects of the successful translation of vision into reality. The impact is visible in several directions at once. Passengers have direct access to major cities; students have a more practical route to institutions and examinations; tourists have an affordable gateway; traders receive bulk consignments closer to market; construction and food supplies move with greater capacity; and flowers, crafts and other local products gain a pathway towards national consumers.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white">The deeper significance of Sairang lies in what it has made possible. A railway line built through difficult hills has compressed distance, widened choice and given Mizoram a new logistics identity. It has linked mobility with dignity, infrastructure with enterprise, and connectivity with opportunity.</span></span></span></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image009_20260913113138_4c89c0.jpg" style="height:237px; width:624px" /></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:white"><strong>(The Sairang-AnandVihar Terminal Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram a direct premium connection with the national capital)</strong></span></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong><img src="https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/image/2026/sep/image010_20260913113150_cdff01.jpg" style="height:372px; width:496px" /></strong></span></span></p>

<p style="margin-left:0cm; margin-right:0cm; text-align:center"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>(The Sairang Railway Bridge has a pier of height 114m, which is 42 m taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar)</strong></span></span></p>
